name: Tunnel Subaortic Stenosis

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Echocardiographic and Hemodynamic Diagnostic Criteria for Tunnel Subaortic Stenosis

criteria.description: Echocardiographic identification of a fibromuscular tunnel-like narrowing of the left ventricular outflow tract
Elevated left ventricular outflow tract pressure gradient ≥50 mmHg on Doppler echocardiography
No significant aortic valve leaflet thickening or calcification to explain obstruction
Cardiac MRI confirming tunnel morphology and excluding other causes of subaortic obstruction

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of echocardiographic evidence of tunnel-like subaortic narrowing with elevated pressure gradient and absence of valvular stenosis
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis relies primarily on imaging modalities; invasive hemodynamic assessment may be used in ambiguous cases.

pathognomonic.symptomName: Systolic ejection murmur localized to the left lower sternal border
searchTerms: heart murmur heard at left lower sternum
abnormal heart sound at left sternal border

pathognomonic.symptomName: Exertional dyspnea due to left ventricular outflow obstruction

searchTerms: feeling of fast or irregular heartbeats

occasional.symptomName: Left ventricular hypertrophy detected on ECG
searchTerms: left ventricular hypertrophy on heart tracing
enlarged left heart muscle detected electrically

occasional.symptomName: Heart failure symptoms including peripheral edema
searchTerms: heart failure with swelling in legs
symptoms of heart failure including leg swelling
heart murmur that spreads to neck arteries
abnormal heart sound heard in carotid area

rare.symptomName: Infective endocarditis involving the subaortic tunnel
Aortic regurgitation secondary to tunnel distortion

laboratory: Normal routine blood tests; possible elevated BNP in heart failure
imaging: Echocardiography showing fibromuscular tunnel-like narrowing of LVOT
Doppler echocardiography demonstrating elevated LVOT pressure gradient
Cardiac MRI confirming tunnel morphology and excluding other lesions
genetic: No specific genetic mutation identified; may be sporadic or familial in rare cases
other: Cardiac catheterization may confirm pressure gradient and anatomy

distinguishingFeatures: Discrete fibrous ridge rather than tunnel-like narrowing
Obstruction at valve level rather than subvalvular
Asymmetric septal hypertrophy without fixed tunnel
Dynamic obstruction with systolic anterior motion of mitral valve

redFlags: Sudden cardiac arrest or unexplained sudden death in young patient
references: Maron BJ, et al. Subaortic stenosis: clinical and surgical considerations. Circulation. 2017.
Gatzoulis MA, et al. Congenital Heart Disease in Adults. Wiley-Blackwell, 2010.
